core_obligations: Derive from the hypotheses, via lemma-precompose-property-local-source and lemma-pullback-property-local-target, that P is stable under precomposing with smooth morphisms and under smooth base change (proof lines 3037-3044).
Unpack part (3)(b) of the definition: for every x there are smooth a_x : U_x \to X, b_x : V_x \to Y and h_x : U_x \to V_x with f \circ a_x = b_x \circ h_x and h_x having P (proof lines 3046-3056).

Assemble U = \coprod U_x, V = \coprod V_x, h = \coprod h_x into the commutative square with a, b smooth and a surjective; note h has P by smooth locality on the target; conclude b \circ h has P by postcomposition stability with the smooth b; finally descend to f along the surjective smooth a by smooth locality on the source (proof lines 3057-3070).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the defining square of part (3) of the definition.
Coproduct the local charts into a single diagram.
Descend P along the surjective smooth a using the two stability facts.
difficulty_reason: The proof first derives stability under precomposition with smooth morphisms and under smooth base change from two cited locality lemmas, then does a genuine diagram chase: given f : X \to Y satisfying part (3)(b) of the definition, it covers X by the smooth charts U_x \to X, takes coproducts U = \coprod U_x, V = \coprod V_x, h = \coprod h_x, notes h has P because P is smooth local on the target, and descends P from b \circ h (which has P by postcomposition stability) along the surjective smooth a using smooth locality on the source. The coproduct assembly and the two descent steps are the substance.
